[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Docker Compose Specification and Profiles"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Docker Compose is an essential tool for defining and running multi-container Docker applications. As your application architecture grows, managing optional services like databases, debugging tools, or testing frameworks can become cumbersome. This tutorial explores the Docker Compose Specification and Profiles, a powerful feature that allows you to conditionally enable or disable services in your compose file."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Compose Profiles"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Profiles allow you to assign services to one or more named groups. When you run docker compose up, only the services that match the active profiles are started. If a service does not have a profile defined, it starts by default. Services with profiles only start when explicitly requested."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Multi-Profile Compose File"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Consider a web application that requires a primary web server and a database. For local development, you might want to include a phpMyAdmin container, and for testing, a separate mock service. Here is how you can use the profiles attribute in your docker-compose.yml file:"},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"version: "3.8"

services:
  web:
    image: nginx:latest
    ports:
      - "80:80"

  database:
    image: postgres:14
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secretpassword

  phpmyadmin:
    image: phpmyadmin/phpmyadmin
    profiles:
      - "debug"
      - "admin"
    ports:
      - "8080:80"

  loadtest:
    image: loki/loadtest
    profiles:
      - "test""},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Running Services with Specific Profiles"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"By default, running docker compose up will start the "web" and "database" services because they do not have any profiles assigned. The "phpmyadmin" and "loadtest" services will be ignored."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"To start default services only: docker compose up"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"To start default services plus the debug profile: docker compose --profile debug up"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"To enable multiple profiles simultaneously: docker compose --profile debug --profile test up"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Enabling Profiles via Environment Variables"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can also specify active profiles permanently using the COMPOSE_PROFILES environment variable in a .env file located in the same directory as your docker-compose.yml file."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"COMPOSE_PROFILES=debug,admin"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"With this configuration in place, running simply docker compose up will automatically spin up the core services as well as the phpmyadmin container without requiring explicit command-line flags."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Docker Compose profiles streamline the development lifecycle by enabling a single compose file to serve multiple environments, from production-like testing to heavy debugging. By leveraging profiles, you keep your configurations clean, modular, and easy to maintain."}]
